div.head: Introduction
div.p: VICAV-compatible datasets are made of TEI documents which share a set of common data type, i.e. a similar structure and comparable content. These can be:

list.label: Feature Lists
list.item: sentence pairs in English and Arabic
list.label: Sample Texts
list.item: translations of the same source text
list.label: Unmonitored Speech
Dictionaries
Profiles
list.item: short sketches of varieties of spoken (contemporary) Arabic
list.label: Bibliographies
list.item: a (full or partial) copy of the VICAV bibliography
list.label: Paratexts
list.item: any other descriptive text (project descriptions, etc.)

div.p: Next to these default data types, projects can define their own specific type of data which can be published via VICAV (see below).

Since the main content of a VICAV-compatible data set is contained within those documents, they are called "Data Documents" in contrast to the "Corpus Document" which holds corpus-wide metadata and points to all the available "Data Documents" in a VICAV dataset.

div.head: Referencing the data type taxonomy
div.p: Each VICAV data document should declare its type. by means of a catRef element within teiHeader/profileDesc/textClass pointing to the relevant catDesc element in this document OR a project-specific definition in the project's corpus document.

In order to avoid identifier conflicts, the ids of dataset-specific data types should be prefixed with the project name, e.g. datatypes.tunocent.tun. The default VICAV data types are prefixed with datatypes.vicav, e.g. datatypes.vicav.st
Please note that the datatype identies must only contain lowercase characters and dots

div.head: Data Document references
div.p: In its body, each TEI element in the corpus document should contain references to the data document(s) derived from it in the data set:

list.item: xi:include element pointing to all TEI documents contained in the data set

div.p: If a recording has been reworked into a properly-encoded TEI document (e.g. a sample text or a feature list document), the stub in the corpus document points to the respective TEI document it its body:

ab.note: The content of this recording has been processed into a TEI document.

div.p: To make target resolvable, there should be a prefixDef for each datatype with the URI prefix equal to the datatype's identifier. If a referenced text/datapoint is embedded within a larger TEI document, the reference could be via a fragment identifier:

prefixDef.p: Private URIs using the datatypes.vicav.st prefix are pointers to VICAV sample texts.

div.p: In case the referenced datapoint / text is a stand-alone TEI document, it should include a reference to the filename as well.

prefixDef.p: Private URIs using the datatypes.vicav.st prefix are pointers to VICAV sample texts.
